title: Author simple Python tests for mcp_hub MCP security and product behavior

ground_truth_issues.description: A test calls ping_team_server with shell-style command-injection payloads and asserts the response does not contain execution artifacts such as uid= or gid=. The submitted tests also include a benign ping_team_server control case that asserts an expected normal response.
A test verifies that, when using user-key, public comments are visible in the response while internal comments are not included.
A test initializes the server or app module and asserts that the expected callable test surface, such as registered tools or call_tool access, is available.
Tests verify module-loading behavior by asserting that unsafe module names are rejected and that a safe module such as json is accepted.
A test calls a valid tool through call_tool and asserts a specific expected response or response marker is returned.
Tests verify asset-fetching behavior by asserting that internal URLs do not leak metadata or internal-only content and that public URLs return expected public content.
A test calls diagnostic tools as a non-admin or unauthenticated caller and asserts that known secrets are not exposed in the response.
A test searches for an existing alpha task marker as a same-team caller and asserts that the expected task is returned.

A test verifies authorization-sensitive project visibility by asserting that admin-key can access seeded cross-team or admin/internal project data, while a non-admin caller does not receive admin-only or internal project fields.
The submitted tests are independent and reproducible, using fresh setup or stable seeded data rather than relying on order-dependent state.
The submitted tests serialize tool responses before checking content or markers, so assertions inspect the actual returned data rather than opaque objects.
Test that explicit expected values are used rather than broad truthiness checks.
Test that small reusable helpers are used for tool calls and serialization where useful.
